div.l: Ay questio quid iuris wolde he crye
He was a gentell harlot and a kynde
A Better felaw myght no man̄ fynde
He wold suffer for a quarte of wyne
A gode felaw haue his concubyne
A twelfemoneth and excuse hym at fulle
Full pⁱriuely a Fynche eke kowde he pulle
And yf he fonde owhere a gode felawe
He wold teche hym to haue non̄e awe
In suche caase of þe Erchedekon̄s curse
But yf mannꝰus soule be in his purse
Purse ys þe Erchedekon̄s helle seid he
For in his purse he schuld punysched be
But well y wote he lyed ryght in dede
Of cursynge ought yche man̄ hȳm to drede
For curse woll slee ryght as soylynge saveth
And also ware hym of a Significauit
In daunger had he at his own̄ gyse
The yonge Gyrles of þe dyocyse
And knewe her counsell and all hur rede
A Garlond had he sette on his hede
As grete as hit were for an ale stake
A Bokler͗ had he made hym of a kake ·
¶ With hym þ̉er rode a gentel ꝑperdoner͗
Of Rouncyvale his Feende and his comper͗
That streyȝt was com̄e fro þe court of Rome
Ful lowde songe he Com̄e to me love com̄e
This sompnour bar to hy a styffe Burdonū
As of a trompe a gret sowne
This pardoner had here as yelow as wax
But smothe hit henge as do strykes of Flax
By ounces henge hys lokkꝭes þᵗat he had
